column1: # Names this tree may use in public text — the registry `validate-public-references.sh` decides by.
# A repository must not be named here unless it is *published*: the allowlist is the check, so a
# name that is not public must not appear in this file either. That is the whole design — the
# private-side denylist cannot live in a public repository, but the complement can.
#   token     the name as it appears in text; a `*` glob registers a family
#   kind      repository | artifact | workspace-package | proposed-crate | rejected | identifier
#               repository        a published GitHub repository — evidence REQUIRED, see below
#               artifact          a published package (crate / npm / PyPI / Maven)
#               workspace-package a crate in this workspace that is not published
#               proposed-crate    a crate name an ADR considered, published nowhere
#               rejected          a name the tree mentions in order to say "not this"
#               identifier        a fixture, env prefix, hook name or script name — no owner
#   evidence  why this name is public, or what it is. A bare assertion is not evidence: every
#             `repository` row carries the command that was run and its result, and the checker
#             refuses a row that does not.
# Measurement date for every row below: 2026-11-11.
# A `repository` row is why a token passes. If a repository is made private, delete its row and
# the guard names every place the tree still says it.
